title: Selling Plans Billing Note — The Term Change Fee
content:
**Billing note.** On **Selling Plans**, the term change fee repays the annual-term saving: it is the plan's monthly term fee less its annual term monthly fee, times the number of regular subscription charges billed on the annual term in the current term, times the repayment share, rounded to the nearest cent; the repayment share is one. The regular charges of the current term are those billed in the whole months from the term start date through the decision date.

## Quantities

| Quantity | Where it comes from |
|---|---|
| Monthly saving | The plan's monthly term fee less the plan's annual term monthly fee, both from the plan's subscription schedule |
| Regular charges of the current term | The subscription fee records of the regular charge type billed on the annual term in the whole months from the term start date through the decision date |
| Repayment share | One |

The three are multiplied together and the product is rounded to the nearest cent once, at the end.

## Worked example (hypothetical plan and dates)

A Basic Store held on the annual term since 10 January; the decision date is 20 May of the same year. Regular annual-term subscription charges were billed on 10 January, 10 February, 10 March, 10 April and 10 May: five charges.

- Monthly saving: USD 27.95 less USD 21.95 is USD 6.00.
- Fee: 6.00 times five times one is USD 30.00.

## Basis Q&A

**Do upgrade proration charges count?** No. Only regular subscription charges billed on the annual term in the current term are counted.

**Do charges of an earlier annual term count?** No. The count runs from the start date of the current term.
